VI.}}</noinclude>house, and it could not moue it: for it vvas founded vpon a rocke. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=49}}† But he that heareth, and doeth not: is like to a man building his house vpon the earth vvithout a foundation: against the vvhich the riuer did beate: and incontinent it fell, and the ruine of that house vvas great.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. VI.}}}}

''3. Neither this haue you read.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Heretikes vnderstād not the Scriptures.}}The Scribes and pharisees boasted most of their knowledge of the Scriptures: but our Sauiour often shevveth their great ignorance. Euen so the Heretikes that novv a daies vaunt most of the Scriptures and of their vnderstanding of them, may soone be proued to vnderstand litle or nothing.

''9. Saue a soule.''] Hereby it seemeth that Christ (as at other times lightly alvvaies) did not only heale this man in body, but of some correspondent disease in his soule.

''12. The whole night.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Churches praiers at the times of giuing holy Orders.}}Our Sauiour instantly prayed, alone in the mount without doore, al night long, as a preparation to the designement of his Apostles the day after: to giue example to the Church of praying instantly vvhen priests are to be ordered, and a lesson to vs al what vve should doe for our ovvne necessities, vvhen Christ did so for other mens.

''13. Whom he named Apostles.''] Here it is to be noted against our Aduersaries that deceitfully measure to the simple the vvhole nature and qualitie of certaine sacred functions, by the primitiue signification and compasse of the names or vvordes vvhereby they be called. vvith vvhom as a Priest is but an elder, and a Bishop, a watchman or Superintendent, so an Apostle is nothing but a Legate or Messenger, and therfore (as they argue) {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Calu. Inst. li. 4 c. 8''.}}can make no Lawes nor prescribe or teach any thing not expressed in his ''mandatum''. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The name and dignitie of Apostles.}}Know therfore against such deceiuers, that such things are not to be ruled by the vulgar signification of the word or calling, but by vse and application of the holy writers, and in this point by Christs ovvne expresse imposition. And so this word, ''Apostle'', is a calling of Office, gouernement, authoritie, and most high dignitie giuen by our Maister, specially to the College of the Twelue: Whom he endued aboue that which the vulgar etymologie of their name requireth, vvith povver to bind and loose, to punish and pardon, to teach and rule his Church. Out of vvhich roome and dignitie, vvhich is called in the Psalme {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 108, 8''.}}and in the actes, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 1, 20.''}}a Bishoprike, vvhen Iudas fel, Mathias vvas chosen to supply it, and vvas numbered among the rest, vvho vvere as founders or foundations of our religion, as the Apostle termeth them, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Eph. 2, 20''.}}Therfore to that college this name agreeth by special imposition and prerogatiue, though aftervvard it vvas by vse of the Scriptures extended to S. Paul and S. Barnabas, and sometimes to the Apostles successors: as also (by the like vse of Scriptures) {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 14. 1. Cor. 12. Eph. 4, 11. 1. Cor. 9, 2. Phil. 2, 25.''}}to the first conuerters of countreis to the faith, or their coadiutors in that function. In vvhich sense S. Paul chalengeth to be the Corinthians Apostle, and nameth Epaphroditus the Philippians Apostle: as vve call S. Gregorie & his Disciple S. Augustin, our Apostles of England. In al vvhich taking, it euer signifieth dignitie, regiment, Paternitie, Principalitie, and Primacie in the Church of God: according to S. Paul 1. Cor. 12. ''He hath placed in his Church, first in deede Apostles &c''. Whereby vve may see that S. Peters dignitie vvas a wonderful eminent Prerogatiue and Soueraintie, When he was the head not only of other Christian men, but the head of al Apostles, yea euen of the College of the Twelue. And if our Aduersaries list to haue learned any profitable lesson by the vvord Apostle, more profitably and truely they might haue gathered, that Christ called these his principal officers, ''Apostles'', or ''Sent'' (him self also specially and aboue al other being ''Missus'', that is, ''Sent'', {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 4, 18.''}}and called also Apostle in the Scriptures) {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Hebr. 3, 1.''}}to vvarne vs by the nature of the vvord, that none are true Apostles, Pastors, or Preachers, that are not specially sent and called, or that can not shew by vvhom they be sent. and that al Heretikes therfore be rather Apostates then Apostles, for that they be not sent, nor duely called, nor chosen to preach.

''14. Simon.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Peters preeminence.}}Peter in the numbering of the Apostles, alvvaies first named and preferred before Andrevv his elder brother and senior by calling, See ''Annotat. Mt. 10, 2''.

''23. Be glad.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Al persecution for Christ, is a blessing.}}The common miseries that fall to the true preachers and other Catholike men for Christs sake, as pouertie, famin, mourning, and persecutions, be in deede the greatest blessings that can be, and are meritorious of the revvard of heauen. Contrarievvise, al the felicities of this vvorld without Christ, are in deede nothing but vvo, and the enterance to euerlasting miserie.

''26. Shal blesse you.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The vanitie of Heretical preachers.}}This vvo pertaineth to the Heretikes of our daies, that delight to haue the peoples praises and blessings and shoutes, preaching pleasant things of purpose to their itching<noinclude>{{rh|||eares:}}</noinclude>
